sections.feature: the scarecrow field, and the hay-bale maze
sections.caption: A scarecrow in a field of fence posts. He looks very pleased with himself. Then hay bales, stacked into a maze that has never once fooled a goat.

sections.feature: the stepping-stone ford, and the old mill pond
sections.caption: A shallow ford, stepping stones worn smooth by a thousand small boots. Beyond it, a mill pond, flat and green, with a wheel that turns for the fun of it.

sections.feature: the lone apple tree, and the hedge-row lane
sections.caption: One apple tree in a ring of clover. The apples are not for you. Probably. A tidy hedge-row lane follows, trimmed by someone with strong opinions.

sections.feature: the beehive meadow, and the berry patch
sections.caption: Humming from every direction. The bees have a no-visitors sign they can't spell. Past the hives, a berry patch, mostly eaten already by someone small.

sections.feature: the hollow log bridge, and the old well
sections.caption: A fallen log, mossy and wide enough for two gnomes who like each other. Then a well with a wooden lid. Knock, and something polite knocks back.

sections.feature: the clover crossroads, and the picnic rise
sections.caption: A signpost with four arrows, all of them pointing at lunch. A grassy rise with a flat spot that is clearly for sitting on.

sections.feature: the wildflower slope, and the dandelion drift
sections.caption: Wildflowers up to your knees, all nodding hello. Then a drift of dandelions. Sneeze, and make a hundred wishes at once.

sections.feature: the little stone bridge, and the beanpole garden
sections.caption: A stone bridge over a trickle you could step over. The bridge insists. Beanpoles stand in tidy rows, and every bean is talking about the weather.

sections.feature: the windmill, and the hay wagon
sections.caption: A windmill with its sails going round, grinding nothing at all. A hay wagon, parked for ever, with a family of sparrows in the driving seat.

sections.feature: the oak-root arch, and the hollow trunk
sections.caption: Roots arch overhead like a doorway someone grew on purpose. Then a hollow trunk you can walk right through, if you duck, and don't mind a spider's hello.

sections.feature: the acorn drop, and the owl-hole oak
sections.caption: Acorns plink down at random. Wear a hat, or don't, they're only small. An old oak with a round hole high up. Someone inside is saying 'hoo' in a sleepy way.

sections.feature: the white-bark tunnel, and the birch curtain
sections.caption: White-barked trees stand close, like friends sharing one big secret. Then a curtain of birch trunks, all in a row, like a crowd that has forgotten why it came.

sections.feature: the fern hollow, and the sunbeam clearing
sections.caption: A fern hollow, soft as a green pillow. A small snail has the best seat. Then a clearing where the sun lands in a square, and a rabbit is sitting in it.

sections.feature: the mossy log, and the drip-stone grotto
sections.caption: A log furred in moss. You wouldn't call it a bridge. It would. Then a small grotto where the drips keep time, more or less.

sections.feature: the mossy gate, and the toadstool steps
sections.caption: Two mossy gateposts and no gate. The moss says that's on purpose. Then big flat toadstools, like stepping stones up a green stair.

sections.feature: the long tideline, and the barnacle rocks
sections.caption: The tide has gone out and left its homework: a long line of shells. Then rocks crusted with barnacles, which all look like they're smiling.

sections.feature: the shell hollow, and the sandcastle shallows
sections.caption: A scoop in the rocks, lined with shells, that echoes if you say 'hello'. Then shallows with a sandcastle: six towers, one flag, and a crab in charge.

sections.feature: the pebble bar, and the kelp line
sections.caption: Pebbles in every colour, all smooth, all lovely to hold. Then a long line of kelp, left by the tide, to be admired and politely not eaten.

sections.feature: the rock pool, and the tide-pool steps
sections.caption: A rock pool with a crab inside who waves one claw. Wave back. Then steps of black rock, each holding a pool the size of a teacup.

sections.feature: the frozen pond, and the snowman gallery
sections.caption: A frozen pond, polished like a plate. Gnomes walk round it. Mostly. Then a row of snowmen, each with a different, very serious carrot.

sections.feature: the icicle cave mouth, and the aurora-glass ledge
sections.caption: A cave mouth fringed with icicles, like a very cold, very polite smile. Then a ledge of clear ice where the sky shows through, pink and green.

sections.feature: the snowdrift pass, and the sled track
sections.caption: Snow piled in steep drifts. Take the zig, then the zag, then the zig. Then a sled track worn smooth by small cheerful gnomes, and one lost mitten.

sections.feature: the snow-comb ridge, and the icicle curtain
sections.caption: A ridge like a comb, with all its teeth pointing politely down. Then a curtain of icicles that chime when you pass. Please don't lick them.

sections.feature: the maple tap row, and the bucket stacks
sections.caption: Rows of maple trees, each with a little bucket. Drip, drip, drip. Then stacks of buckets, waiting for the sap to get its act together.

sections.feature: the Sugar Shack yard, and the pancake lane
sections.caption: A little sugar shack with a chimney that smells of pancakes. Then a lane that smells so strongly of pancakes it is hard to walk straight.

sections.feature: the ring-count log, and the woodpecker tree
sections.caption: A fallen log with its rings showing. Count them. Then lose count. Start again. Then a tall dead tree where a woodpecker is knocking out a very slow song.

sections.feature: the toadstool ring, and the bramble corridor
sections.caption: Toadstools in a perfect ring. Step inside and you feel exactly one inch taller. Then brambles on both sides, and the berries are right there. You may have one.

sections.feature: the great stump, and the squirrel's larder
sections.caption: A stump as wide as a house. Its rings go back before your grandmother's grandmother. Then acorns hidden in every nook. The squirrel will pretend not to watch.

sections.feature: the beaver dam, and the mud slide
sections.caption: A beaver dam, tidy as a drawer. Walk the top or the bottom; both ways are damp. Then a muddy bank, shiny as a plum, where somebody has clearly been sliding for fun.

sections.feature: the beaver lodge, and the stick gate
sections.caption: The beaver lodge, a dome of sticks. Someone is cooking in there. Smells like bark stew. Then a gate made entirely of sticks, with a latch made of a smaller stick.

sections.feature: the tunnel mouth, and the glow-cap tunnel
sections.caption: A hillside with a round dark doorway and a tiny 'Welcome' sign, hung slightly crooked. Then mushrooms glow softly along the walls. They are shy, but not unfriendly.

sections.feature: the driftwood beach, and the shell pile
sections.caption: Driftwood in lovely shapes: a dragon, a chair, a very tired sofa. Then a heap of shells, sorted by someone with very strong feelings about spirals.

sections.feature: the tidal causeway, and the stepping rocks
sections.caption: A causeway of flat stones with the tide lapping both sides. Nobody has fallen in. Nobody who'll admit it. Then dark flat rocks to hop between, with the sea sloshing happily underneath.

sections.feature: the lantern rocks, and the gull parliament
sections.caption: Tall rocks with a lantern in each, lit by something that sounds like humming. Then a rock where a hundred gulls sit in rows, mid-way through a very important meeting.

to: Den of the Great White Owl

sections.feature: the snowy gate, and the lamp-post lane
sections.caption: Two snowy gateposts and a sign that just says 'Owl? Yes.' Then a lane of lamp-posts, each with a warm yellow bulb and one snowflake on its hat.

sections.feature: the pine slope, and the snow fort
sections.caption: Pines in rows like a sleeping crowd. The snow slides off their shoulders with a soft 'fwump'. Then a snow fort with walls knee-high, built by someone very serious about it.

sections.feature: the frozen stream, and the icicle bridge
sections.caption: A stream gone to glass, crossed by one bridge of packed snow. Then a bridge of packed snow over a ditch of blue shadow. Sturdier than it looks.

sections.feature: the giant feather, and the feather cairns
sections.caption: A single white feather the size of a gnome, standing in the snow like a flag. Then little cairns of stones, each topped with a feather. Someone has been very patient.

sections.feature: the owl's den, and the owl's doorstep
sections.caption: A wide round den under a snowy hill, with two big kind eyes inside, blinking slowly. Then a doormat made of moss, and a very big, very soft 'hoo' from just ahead.

sections.feature: the sky-watch hill, and the star-chart stones
sections.caption: A round hill with a flat top, perfect for lying down and counting nothing in particular. Then flat stones laid in the shape of the sky, so you can look down at the stars.

sections.feature: the aurora camp, and the kettle tree
sections.caption: Tents, a banked fire and a kettle, with green lights doing slow dances overhead. Then a tree hung with kettles and mugs, clinking. Whoever lives here is always ready for tea.
